control: Democrats win control, 26-24: AP race calls, per The Philadelphia Inquirer at 9:43 a.m. ET Wednesday. Republicans held it 27-23 before.
basis: Inquirer report of AP race calls: Democrats flipped SD-6, SD-16, SD-24 and SD-40; Republicans won SD-36. Applied to the earlier 24-24 Inquirer tally with SD-16 and SD-40 then uncalled, that gives 26-24.
official: Certification pending: counties must certify by Nov. 23.

control: Democrats keep the majority: 111 seats with a reported winner, more than the 102 needed; Republicans 89, three races uncalled (HD-41, HD-143, HD-147).
basis: Counts only districts with a reported winner or a concession (MultiState district list, read 5:27 p.m. ET Thursday, plus WPXI report of the HD-12 concession): 111 D, 89 R, 3 undecided (HD-41, 143, 147). Nine of the 111 are reported Republican-to-Democratic flips (HD-13, 18, 44, 88, 131, 137, 142, 160, 187); HD-18, 44, 88, 131, 137, 160 and 187 have AP calls in our sources (WPXI, PublicSource, Armchair Lehigh Valley); HD-13 and HD-142 have no call named yet. HD-12 is a Democratic-to-Republican flip on Rep. Brandon Dukes's concession (WPXI). Check: 103 D before, plus 9 flips, minus HD-12 = 111; 100 R before, minus 9, plus HD-12, minus HD-41, 143 and 147 (R-held, undecided) = 89. 111 + 89 + 3 = 203. Spotlight PA (12:07 p.m. ET Friday) reports AP had called 111 races for Democrats, that Democrats in HD-143 and HD-147 have declared victory, and that HD-41 is the only legislative race still too close to call.
official: Certification pending: counties must certify by Nov. 23.

matchup: Brad Chambers (D) vs. Brett Miller (R, incumbent)
called_by: Not called: no AP or network call found; FOX43 earlier reported AP listed the race as too close to call
note: Unofficial: after Lancaster County counted 139 provisional ballots Friday, Chambers 14,289, Miller 14,259, a 30-vote Chambers lead (LancasterOnline, 12:37 p.m. ET Friday); election-night count had Miller ahead 14,225 to 14,184. PoliticsPA (1:14 p.m. ET Friday) reports Chambers won 105 of the 139 provisional votes. Still outstanding: 7 challenged provisional ballots and up to 14 overseas/military ballots that can arrive until 5 p.m. Tuesday; the county board hears provisional challenges Thursday, Nov. 12. LancasterOnline describes the lead as appearing insurmountable, but no AP or network call and no concession has been reported. A recount would need three voters per precinct to petition the Court of Common Pleas. Spotlight PA and The Sentinel (Friday) report the race is still too close to call; Chambers said his campaign "will accept the final results once they are available," and the Miller campaign and the House Republican Campaign Committee did not respond to requests for comment. LancasterOnline (about 3:30 p.m. ET Friday): Chambers declared victory on social media; the seven challenged provisional ballots lacked a required poll-worker signature and the board hears them at 11:30 a.m. Thursday; the Miller campaign could petition Lancaster County Court for a recount within five days of the count being completed. No concession and no AP or network call reported.

detail: Spent June 8 to Oct. 19, the most for that window in a decade (2024: $36.5 million). House Democrats about $20 million, Senate Democrats $12 million, Senate Republicans nearly $10 million, House Republicans $8 million.
Gave $2.5 million to Senate President Pro Tempore Kim Ward's accounts and funded the two committees below.

group: PA Education Choice Fund (sole donor: Students First)
detail: Aug. to mid-Oct. gifts to Sens. Frank Farry (SD-6), Tracy Pennycuick (SD-24) and Rosemary Brown (SD-40): 50% to 80% of their fundraising in that period.

group: Commonwealth Children's Choice Fund (run by Matt Brouillette)
detail: Received $5.5 million from Students First; also gave $1.3 million to the Yass-affiliated Commonwealth Leaders Fund.

amount: Nearly $7.8 million to Pa. legislative candidates
detail: Raised $20.1 million this year, mostly from blue-state donors including Jonathan Soros and Lynn Schusterman. Backed Hadley Haas (HD-44), Sara Agerton (HD-88), Elizabeth Moro (HD-160) and independent Jodi Borello (SD-46).

group: First Amendment LLC (paid super PAC Make Liberty Win)
detail: Top independent spender: mail, calls and digital ads against Democrats in 20 House and 6 Senate races. Make Liberty Win is funded with $40 million from venture capitalist Scott Banister.

Ads in 11 House and 5 Senate races. Raised $8 million, nearly half from PA Alliance Action, a dark money nonprofit that does not disclose donors, plus $1.2 million from the federal dark money group American Leadership Committee.

group: Pennsylvania Chamber of Business and Industry
detail: Independent expenditures in legislative races.
Per Department of State records as of Nov. 2. Final totals come with post-election finance reports.
Campaign funds Shapiro spent to help Democrats win the legislature, per The Washington Post as cited in PoliticsPA's Nov. 5 Playbook.
disclosure: Reported by news; itemized figures come with post-election finance reports.
